Verbatim copies of selected TRForge modules (MIT licensed, see LICENSE).

DO NOT EDIT THESE FILES. The first three header lines of a TRForge module
carry a hidden signature (an acrostic); reformatting destroys it. Anything
this project needs differently is written in our own wrappers under
TOMB5\specific\hd\, never in here.

Taken  : 2026-09-05, for #123 stage S0 (HD at run time)

WHAT WAS DELIBERATELY NOT TAKEN, and why

    Dds.cpp / Dds.h        we have our own BC7 decoder, specific\bc7.cpp,
                           which the diagnostic tool DdsProbe already proves.
    ItemModels.h / .cpp    the .TRM reader. Its header includes
                           trf_level\Level.h (for bind_level_items) and
                           trf_remaster\Remaster.h, so a verbatim copy drags
                           in the whole trf_level branch - which #123's plan
                           rules out. The .TRM side therefore lives in our
                           own translation unit, specific\hd\hd_trm.cpp,
                           which credits TRForge for the format.
    Remaster.h / .cpp      same case: the header includes trf_assets\Image.h
                           and trf_remaster\Dds.h, the source includes
                           trf_level\Level.h and TrgTiles.h. The three parts
                           we need (install layout, LEVELn.MAP, sidecar
                           names) are a few dozen lines and are written in
                           specific\hd\hd_install.cpp and hd_bind.cpp.
    trf_level, trf_assets, trf_editor
                           not needed: our engine already holds the classic
                           level in memory, in its randomized state.

LANGUAGE STANDARD. Trg.cpp uses <filesystem>, so these files are compiled as
C++17 (per-file <LanguageStandard> in tomb5.vcxproj); the rest of the engine
keeps the project default. Nothing here crosses a translation unit boundary
with an STL type - specific\hd\hd_level.h is plain C-shaped on purpose.
